vulnerability: Incorrect reserve storage update for odd-length token arrays causes accumulation and permanent DoS/locked funds.
reason: The odd-length branch of storeUint128 incorrectly adds the new last reserve to the existing low 128 bits of the storage slot instead of overwriting it. The expression shr(128, shl(128, sload(add(slot, maxI)))) extracts the current low 128 bits and adds them to the new reserve. As a result, every _setReserves call for a Well with an odd number of tokens stores newReserve + oldReserve for the last token. After the second reserve update, the stored last reserve becomes inflated beyond the actual token balance. The next _setReserves check (reserves[i] <= token.balanceOf) will fail because the memory reserves read from storage already exceed the actual balance. This permanently bricks the Well for swaps, add/remove liquidity, and most other operations, locking all deposited funds. An attacker can deliberately trigger this by performing two small swaps or liquidity operations on any odd-token Well, causing a permanent denial of service and loss of funds for all users. This is exploitable in the real world for any Well with 3, 5, etc., tokens.

vulnerability: Unauthorized withdrawal of surplus reserves via shift allows theft of accumulated fees/donations.
reason: shift computes the excess of a token over the reserve required to maintain the well invariant for the current LP supply and transfers that excess to an arbitrary recipient without burning any LP tokens or requiring the caller to be an LP. If the Well accumulates surplus due to swap fees (from a fee-charging well function), token donations, or rounding, any attacker can call shift with recipient set to themselves and minAmountOut = 0 to steal the entire surplus. This surplus rightfully belongs to existing LP holders. The function has no access control and directly transfers the surplus to the caller-chosen address. This is exploitable in any fee-charging Well or after any accidental token transfer, allowing an attacker to drain value that should accrue to LPs.

vulnerability: Unauthorized minting of LP tokens for surplus reserves via sync dilutes existing LPs and steals surplus.
reason: sync reads the actual token balances, computes the LP token supply corresponding to those balances, and mints the difference to an arbitrary recipient without requiring any deposit. If the Well has surplus reserves (e.g., from swap fees or donations), newTokenSupply will exceed oldTokenSupply, and the difference is minted to the recipient specified by the caller. An attacker can call sync with recipient set to themselves to mint free LP tokens. These LP tokens can then be used to withdraw a proportional share of the pool, effectively stealing the surplus value from existing LPs. The function has no access control and allows any caller to choose the recipient. This is exploitable in any fee-charging Well or after any token donation, allowing an attacker to profit at the expense of existing liquidity providers.
